generated_report: Atelectasis refers to the collapse or closure of a lung resulting in reduced or absent gas exchange. It may affect part or all of one lung. It is usually associated with decreased breath sounds and crackles. Cardiomegaly refers to the enlargement of the heart, which can be due to various conditions such as hypertension, coronary artery disease, or heart valve disorders. Consolidation refers to the filling of the lung's air spaces with fluid, cells, tissue, or other substances, which can be seen in conditions like pneumonia. Pulmonary edema refers to the excess accumulation of fluid in the lungs, often resulting from heart conditions. Pleural effusion is the build-up of excess fluid between the layers of the pleura outside the lungs.
